domain_restrictions: d is a nonnegative integer (so affine d-space means d coordinates; includes the case d = 0)
for each i with 1 <= i <= d, w_i is a positive integer
S is the polynomial ring k[x_1,...,x_d] equipped with weighted grading determined by deg(x_i)=w_i
I is homogeneous with respect to this weighted grading
the zero locus condition is evaluated after base change from k to an algebraic closure kbar
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every field k, every nonnegative integer d, every tuple of positive integers w_1 through w_d, every homogeneous ideal I in the weighted graded polynomial ring S = k[x_1 through x_d] with deg(x_i)=w_i: if the set of common zeros of I in kbar^d (for a fixed algebraic closure kbar of k) is exactly the origin tuple (0,...,0), then the quotient ring S modulo I is finite-dimensional as a vector space over k.
quantifier_order: for all choices of positive integers w_1,...,w_d
for all homogeneous ideals I of the weighted graded ring S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with deg(x_i)=w_i
if (over an algebraic closure kbar of k) the common zero locus of I in affine d-space equals exactly the origin
then S over I is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space

statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_i)=w_i. Let I be a homogeneous ideal of S. If, over an algebraic closure of k, the common zero locus of I in affine d-space is exactly the origin, then S/I is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space.
